english.title: Make or possess PSV operator's licence / fitness or type certificate / disc or control document with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to deceive,

(A)_[made]_
(B)_[possessed]_
(C)_[a document]_
(D)_[**(..SPECIFY THING MADE OR POSSESSED..)]_

so closely resembling

(E)_[a licence under Part II of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981]_
(F)_[a certificate of initial fitness under section 6 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981]_
(G)_[a certificate under section 10 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981 that a vehicle conformed to a type vehicle]_
(H)_[an operator's disc under section 18 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981]_
(I)_[a certificate under section 21 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981 as to the repute, financial standing or professional competence of a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)]_
(J)_[a control document issued in pursuance of regulation 4 of the Road Transport (International Passenger Services) Regulations 2018]]_

as to be calculated to deceive
english.legislation: Contrary to section65(2)(b) of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
with intent to deceive
made / possessed a licence under Part II of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981
or something so closely resembling such a licence as to be calculated to deceive

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) This offence applies from the 1st April 2025 due to changes by SI 2024/1370 Road Transport (International Passenger Services) (Amendment) Regulations 2024. For the offence before this date, see H16538.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: A fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment.

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
